title: Limit preservation makes representable Isom spaces locally of finite type
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme. Work with schemes [def-pc-scheme] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal F$ be a category fibred in groupoids over $S$-schemes: each fibre is a groupoid, with pullback functors and coherent identity and composition isomorphisms. Assume limit preservation: on every small directed inverse system of affine $S$-schemes with limit $T$, objects over $T$ descend to a stage, isomorphisms descend to a sufficiently late common stage, and equality of isomorphisms is detected at a sufficiently late stage. Suppose every presheaf $T'\mapsto\operatorname{Isom}(a|_{T'},b|_{T'})$, for $a,b\in\mathcal F(T)$, is represented by an algebraic space $I_{a,b}$ over $T$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Then every $I_{a,b}\to T$ is locally of finite type. In particular, for schemes $U,V$ locally of finite type over $S$ and objects $x\in\mathcal F(U)$, $y\in\mathcal F(V)$, the triples $(a:T\to U,b:T\to V,\alpha:a^*x\cong b^*y)$ are represented by an algebraic space $Z$, and $Z\to U\times_S V$, $Z\to U$, $Z\to V$, and the composites $W\to Z\to U$ and $W\to Z\to V$ for every etale scheme chart $W\to Z$ are locally of finite type. Locally of finite type for spaces means locally of finite type on compatible etale scheme charts, using [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; $U\times_SV$ is [def-pc-fibre-product], and etale means [def-weil-etale-morphism].

source.place: Tag 0CXI (lemma-diagonal); the fibre-product and chart consequences are the first paragraph of the proof of Tag 0CXM (lemma-base-change-versal).

proof.text: Consider $\Delta:\mathcal F\to\mathcal F\times\mathcal F$. Over a scheme $B$ and a pair $(a,b)$, its base-change groupoid has objects $(c,u:c\xrightarrow{\sim}a,v:c\xrightarrow{\sim}b)$. Send this object to $v u^{-1}\in\operatorname{Isom}(a,b)$. Conversely send $\delta:a\xrightarrow{\sim}b$ to $(a,\mathrm{id},\delta)$. A morphism between two triples, when it exists, is uniquely determined by $u$, and exists exactly when their images $vu^{-1}$ agree. These constructions commute with pullback using the given cartesian coherence. Thus this groupoid is equivalent to the discrete groupoid represented by $I_{a,b}$, naturally on $B$-schemes. The diagonal is therefore representable by algebraic spaces in the precise sense required by [lem-sfb-representable-lfp-object-limit-test].

source.place: Tag 06CX (lemma-representable-by-spaces-limit-preserving), representability hypothesis; explicit diagonal fibre identification

proof.text: Verify the relative object-descent condition of [lem-sfb-representable-lfp-object-limit-test] for $\Delta$. Fix a small nonempty directed affine system $T_i$ with limit $T$, a pair $(a_i,b_i)$ at stage $i$, $c\in\mathcal F(T)$, and $\gamma=(u:c\xrightarrow{\sim}a_i|_T,v:c\xrightarrow{\sim}b_i|_T)$. By the assumed descent of isomorphisms, $\delta=vu^{-1}$ descends to $\delta_j:a_i|_{T_j}\xrightarrow{\sim}b_i|_{T_j}$ for some $j\geq i$. Put $c_j=a_i|_{T_j}$, $\alpha=u^{-1}:c_j|_T\to c$ and $\beta=(\mathrm{id},\delta_j):\Delta(c_j)\to(a_i,b_i)|_{T_j}$. Then $\gamma\Delta(\alpha)=(uu^{-1},vu^{-1})=(\mathrm{id},\delta)=\beta|_T$, exactly the required compatibility. All maps are isomorphisms because the fibres are groupoids. The cited criterion now gives that every $I_{a,b}\to B$ is locally of finite presentation on etale scheme charts. No descent of objects over an arbitrary nonaffine base is being assumed.

source.place: Tag 06CX, implication from relative object descent to local finite presentation; explicit verification using artin.tex Tag 07XL (definition-limit-preserving)

proof.text: A finitely presented algebra $A[t_1,\ldots,t_n]/(f_1,\ldots,f_m)$ is generated as an $A$-algebra by the images of $t_1,\ldots,t_n$. Therefore [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] implies [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] locally. Applying this observation to the same compatible etale scheme charts, with the chart test [lem-sfb-space-local-properties-chart-test], shows that every $I_{a,b}\to B$ is locally of finite type. This uses no quasi-compactness or Noetherian assumption.

source.place: Tag 0464 (lemma-finite-presentation-finite-type), local clause; the finite-generation implication is written out

proof.text: Put $P=U\times_SV$ with projections $p,q$, and $A=p^*x$, $B=q^*y$. By [def-pc-fibre-product], a map $T\to P$ is exactly a pair of $S$-maps $a:T\to U$, $b:T\to V$. By the representing property in the hypothesis, $Z=I_{A,B}$ therefore represents precisely the triples in the statement. Step 3 gives $Z\to P$ locally of finite type. By [lem-sfb-stack-finite-type-calculus], restricted to algebraic spaces (including schemes), $p$ and $q$ are locally of finite type as base changes of $V\to S$ and $U\to S$, respectively, and composition gives $Z\to U$ and $Z\to V$ locally of finite type. For any etale scheme chart $W\to Z$, apply [lem-sfb-space-etale-presentation-property-criterion] with $P$ the local-finite-type property, which is etale local on source-and-target by [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-source-target-properties]. Take the target chart to be the identity of $U$, respectively $V$. Its every-presentation-diagram clause gives $W\to U$ and $W\to V$ locally of finite type even when $W\to Z$ is not surjective.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q103-07100d949 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, every cited statement and the sources: artin.tex Tag 0CXI (lemma-diagonal, which concludes the diagonal is locally of finite type) and criteria.tex Tag 06CX (for representable maps, limit preserving on objects is equivalent to locally of finite presentation). The delivery has no new nodes and leaves the statement and stmt_deps unchanged. Step 1 is a genuinely elementary groupoid calculation: a morphism of triples is forced to be u'^{-1}u and exists iff vu^{-1}=v'u'^{-1}, so the fibre of the diagonal is the discrete Isom functor and the item's Isom hypothesis supplies exactly the representability the criterion lem-sfb-representable-lfp-object-limit-test needs. Step 2 checks relative object descent for the diagonal using only the item's isomorphism descent; I verified the required compatibility with x_j=a_i|T_j, alpha=u^{-1}, beta=(id,delta_j). The criterion then gives local finite presentation. Step 3 forgets the relations to get local finite type and transfers it with lem-sfb-space-local-properties-chart-test, which covers both properties on the same charts. Step 4 is the first paragraph of Tag 0CXM: the fibre-product universal property, base change and composition from lem-sfb-stack-finite-type-calculus (whose statement covers algebraic spaces), and the every-presentation-diagram clause of lem-sfb-space-etale-presentation-property-criterion with target chart the identity of U (respectively V); local finite type is etale local on source and target by lem-sfb-scheme-etale-source-target-properties. Edge cases checked: empty bases, one-stage systems, and no quasi-compactness assumed on U or V. There is no cycle and no duplicate in the DAG, and no SGA is cited. Batch-5 flags: the three algebraic-space nodes reach the trace-formula chapter only through def-trf-algebraic-space, a general definition already in the item's stmt_deps; the scheme etale-locality node reaches it only through lem-trf-smooth-composition, composition of smooth morphisms. Neither is part of the trace formula or Poincare duality, so all four are accepted. The only faults are cosmetic letter reuse (B and P) in step 4, which needs no fix.
